decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts build on the firm's core drilling and bonding know-how, so keeping them costs little while demand for wafer-level packaging still grows.
Carrier wafers for handling smaller diameter wafers fit the firm's stated focus on reusable carriers and are cheap to keep as a catalog item, so the option stays open.
The Cu-interposer is a flagship technology launched at SEMICON in 2019, and its value in advanced packaging is still uncertain but promising, which justifies keeping this growth option.
The off-the-shelf Wafer Universe brand draws on existing standard production at low incremental cost and supports volume sales, so there is no reason to abandon it.

Glass-based circuit boards are further from the core business and their prospects remain uncertain, but the lack of website evidence is no sign of failure and keeping them is cheap, so the option is retained for now.
